stated_purpose: The specification describes a planned real-time web application in which users speak with an animated Abraham Lincoln portrait that answers through historically grounded retrieval, an in-character language model, cloned speech, and lip-synchronized video.

planned_work.statement: The proposed streaming pipeline captures microphone audio, transcribes it with Deepgram, retrieves Lincoln source passages with OpenAI embeddings and FAISS, streams an in-character response from Claude, synthesizes speech with ElevenLabs, and animates a portrait through D-ID.

The planned client is a React application with Web Audio, WebSocket, WebRTC, portrait presentation, and idle, listening, thinking, and speaking states; the planned backend is a FastAPI service that orchestrates the external AI services.

The specification lays out eight implementation phases covering corpus construction, retrieval, persona generation, speech recognition, speech synthesis, avatar animation, orchestration, frontend integration, error handling, and polish.
Future ideas include additional historical figures, conversational memory, emotion detection, 3D animation, museum kiosk packaging, multilingual conversations, and classroom controls.

architecture.statement: The specification defines a browser client connected to a backend conversation WebSocket, with a sequentially dependent but internally streamed STT-to-RAG/LLM-to-TTS-to-avatar data flow and WebRTC delivery for animated video.
The proposed retrieval layer uses a local FAISS IndexFlatIP index over approximately 5,000 chunks of public-domain Lincoln writings, with OpenAI embeddings and top-three retrieval.
The proposed repository layout separates backend pipeline adapters, knowledge ingestion and generated indexes, persona prompts, React components and hooks, WebRTC support, and utility scripts.
None of the specified architecture is present as tracked executable code at this revision.

accomplishments.statement: A 770-line system specification documents the intended experience, service choices, data flow, component responsibilities, persona prompt, environment-variable names, API message shapes, implementation sequence, cost estimates, and test strategy.
The specification identifies streaming as a core design constraint and describes sentence-level buffering intended to overlap language generation, speech synthesis, and animation.
The repository ignores the exact .env filename and contains no tracked credential file or credential value.

gaps.statement: The repository has no source code, corpus, portrait asset, generated index, dependency manifest, container definition, executable entry point, or frontend scaffold.
The documented unit, integration, streaming, latency, and character tests have not been created, and there is no CI or execution evidence.
The target latency, cost estimates, service compatibility, and quality assertions are design assumptions rather than measured properties of this repository.

Operational details such as authentication, authorization, retention of microphone or conversation data, observability, deployment, rate-limit behavior, and concrete failure recovery are not defined beyond brief mentions.

risks.statement: The design depends on five external AI services and several streaming protocols, so undocumented API drift, cross-service buffering, rate limits, or incompatible media formats could prevent the stated latency and end-to-end behavior.
The proposed instruction to clone a Lincoln impersonator's recording introduces consent, licensing, attribution, and misleading-authenticity concerns that are not addressed in the specification.

Microphone audio, transcripts, prompts, and generated media would cross multiple third-party services, but the repository contains no implemented privacy, access-control, deletion, or secret-management safeguards.

The Lincoln persona and retrieval plan lack a documented historical-review or citation mechanism, creating a risk that generated statements could be presented as authentic history without adequate provenance.

suggested_next_actions.statement: Before implementation, validate the current APIs, model identifiers, streaming capabilities, media formats, pricing, and measured latency of the proposed vendors with a minimal end-to-end spike.

Define an MVP acceptance test that proves one question can travel through transcription, retrieval, response generation, speech synthesis, and portrait animation while recording per-stage and end-to-end latency.

Add explicit policies for microphone and transcript retention, third-party data processing, API-key handling, rate limits, failure behavior, and user disclosure that the voice and statements are synthesized.
Resolve licensing and consent for the portrait, historical texts, and any voice-cloning source, and add expert-reviewed provenance or citations for historically grounded answers.

questions: Is this specification still intended for implementation, or was the repository created only to preserve the design exercise?
Which vendor stack and model versions remain preferred after current API, pricing, and latency validation?
What rights or consent will authorize the portrait and voice-cloning source?
Should users receive citations or source excerpts for Lincoln's historical claims?
What privacy and retention requirements apply to microphone audio, transcripts, and generated media?
